notes: The COUNT and the ORDER. DataItem.SubscriptArity is the count - one per OCCURS clause in the item's description, fixed or dynamic - and DataItem.SubscriptLevels() is the same walk as a list, outermost first, which is SR3's 'order of successively less inclusive dimensions'. Five hand-written copies of that ancestor walk were in the compiler; the drift test pins it to one. POSITIVE: the 85 golden writes one subscript per dimension in every position, including the two-dimensional Y2 OF Y-REC (X(1), 2) and the nested SEARCH ALL T-E (T-N (1), TX) whose witness value discriminates the outer occurrence. NEGATIVE: X (1, 2) on a one-dimensional element is COBOL2097 at all four editions. SR5's seven exceptions are all about OMITTING the subscript list and are decided by the owning binders (a SEARCH subject, a REDEFINES clause, an OCCURS KEY IS phrase, a SORT key or table subject, a screen entry's FROM/TO/USING phrase, a report SUM addend), so the screen deliberately fires only on a reference that WRITES subscripts. retired-witness: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/ReferenceResolver.cs#AccessPath (PB2299-PB2375: the member moved with the extraction of ReferenceResolver into NameResolution, RefModBinder, SubscriptBinder, ObjectPropertyResolver, CounterResolver and the model-layer PlaceBuilder) retired-witness: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/ReferenceResolver.cs#ScreenSubscriptArity (PB2299-PB2375: the member moved with the extraction of ReferenceResolver into NameResolution, RefModBinder, SubscriptBinder, ObjectPropertyResolver, CounterResolver and the model-layer PlaceBuilder)
